Subject: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity next steps

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on the high-level goals for PayGrid's document extraction and intent classification flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: validate an open-model baseline that meets your acceptance thresholds vs. your proprietary baseline so we can recommend a serving configuration (hosted vs dedicated) and cost estimate.
- Suggested models to evaluate (initial sweep): Redwood-Open-1.5B-8bit, RW-Open-2.7B-q5, and RW-Open-6B (float16).
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed): >=95% parity on intent recall, <=1% downstream fallback rate for NLU intents, and average inference latency (p95) < 250ms for the configured batch profile.
- Eval scope: 5k labeled prompts (we recommend the attached prompt set v1) covering your top 12 intents + edge cases. We'll run generation + NLU scoring to compute recall/precision and a regression delta vs the baseline you provide.
- Deliverables: summary CSV with metrics, error-case examples (10-15 per intent), and recommended quantization/serving profile.

Attachments: paygrid-prompt-set-v1.txt, paygrid-benchmarks-summary.csv (template). Also shared a Drive folder with the eval artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPayGridEvalDocs

Can you confirm:
1) You can share a small sample of the proprietary baseline outputs (5–10k rows) or the aggregate metrics for recall/precision so we can align the parity calculation.
2) You're comfortable with the 5k prompt eval (we can expand if you want broader coverage).
3) A scoping call with your ML/infra engineer — proposed slot: Fri 2026-07-02 10:00am PT (we'll have Aditya and Marcus join).

If that all looks good, we'll queue the eval on our dedicated test cluster and share a run plan + the eval-run-template.yaml (Aditya included below).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the Friday call: 

- Parity metric: when you say ">=95% parity on intent recall", are you computing parity as (open_model_recall / baseline_recall) * 100, or delta recall thresholds? For example if our baseline recall is 0.92, do you expect open model recall of 0.874 (95% of 0.92) or an absolute delta of -0.03?

- Will Redwood run the eval on hosted infra or do you need us to provide a staging endpoint for the baseline? We prefer Redwood to run everything on dedicated test infra to avoid exposing data to additional endpoints.

We'll share a CSV with anonymized baseline outputs and some aggregate metrics by EOD today. Friday 10am PT should work — Olivia will join.

Also can you confirm the expected artifact turnaround after the run (how soon will we get the summary + examples)?

Thanks,
Samir

Hi all — quick technical notes for the eval run so expectations are aligned: 

- Parity calc: we'll provide both relative parity (open/baseline %) and absolute delta. In your example, we'll report that an open-model recall of 0.874 equals 95% relative parity against baseline 0.92, and separately show absolute delta (-0.046). We find both views helpful when assessing business impact.

- Eval infra: we can run on Redwood Dedicated test cluster (isolated per-account eval). That matches PayGrid's preference and keeps baseline data on our private test pool.

- Config recommendations (attached as eval-run-template.yaml):
  - batch_size: 8 (latency-sensitive path)
  - kv_cache_enabled: true for multi-turn examples
  - quantization: q5_0 for 2.7B, 8-bit for 1.5B as a cost/latency tradeoff
  - eval_metrics: intent_recall, intent_precision, top1_accuracy, latency_p50/p95, token_efficiency (tokens/response)

- Run duration: for 5k prompts with the above config we expect ~45–90 minutes depending on concurrency; deliverables posted within 48 hours after run completion (metrics CSV + 10–15 error cases per notable intent).

I'll drop the eval template in this thread and the Drive folder.

Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir
